sentences.text:
Madan Mohan Tyagi vs The State Of Uttar Pradesh on 18 July,
2023
Bench: Sanjay Kishan Kaul, Sudhanshu Dhulia

1
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal No. 1992/2023
 (Arising out of Slp(Crl.) No. 789/2022)
 Madan Mohan Tyagi & Anr. ..Appellant
 Versus
 The State Of Uttar Pradesh & Anr. ..Respondent
 O
R D E R Leave granted.
In pursuance of the reference of the dispute to mediation a report has been received from the Supreme Court Mediation Centre dated 30.8.2022 enclosing a settlement agreement dated 29.8.2022.
The settlement agreement has been signed by both the parties, their counsel and the mediator.
There is no apparent impediment to acceptance of the settlement and, thus, we accept the settlement and the parties shall remain bound by the settlement.
The settlement enlists the cases to be withdrawn.
There is no child born out of the wedlock.

In view of the settlement the parties have agreed that the husband would pay a sum of Rs.9,00,000/- (Rupees Nine Lakh Only) to the respondent wife as the first installment on the Reason: first motion being passed and Rs.8,75,000/-
(Rupees Eight Lakh Seventy Five Thousand Only) as the final installment on the decree being passed.
We appreciate the role played by the counsel and the mediator and the approach adopted by the parties.
There seems to be, however, a communication gap later on, that is all we can say.
The second motion for mutual consent has been filed and the amount which has to be released to the wife has also been deposited in Court.
The parties will appear before the Court for grant of decree of divorce.
As far as the inter se cases are concerned, the husband has withdrawn the cases while one of the cases filed by the respondent/wife has been dismissed.

There are stated to be other cases pending between the parties which are as under:

1 1) First Appeal No. 253/2022 filed by the husband in High Court of Judicature at Allahabad;
2) Special leave petition filed by the husband bearing SLP(Crl.) No. 789/2022,
pending before this Court,
3) Cases filed by the respondent wife (I) Case No. 63/2018 under the Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (ii) Case No. 317/2018 under Section 125 Cr.P.C.
(iii) Case No. 2701196/2019 under Sections 498A, 352,504, 406, IPC along with Section 3 & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, (iv) Complaint Case No. 6908501/2018 and (v) NCR Report 140/2018 under Sections 323, 508 & 307, IPC.
To put an end to the controversy, we consider appropriate that the details of the cases mentioned aforesaid shall stand quashed/closed.
